reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises: it reports the baseline fcc soft magnetic state, the RTA-induced fcc phase with 40× coercivity increase, the formation of a single L1₀ phase upon 50 at.% Pt addition with RTA, a three-order-of-magnitude coercivity increase, and attributes the anisotropy to symmetry reduction and Pt spin–orbit coupling. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings, though it extends the claim to FeCoNi (without MnCu) and specifies a 15 s pulse, which are minor extrapolations from the cited work.
premises: Sputtered FeCoNiMnCu films are initially fcc and magnetically soft (~10 Oe).
RTA alone on FeCoNiMnCu yields a single fcc phase with ~40× coercivity increase.
Adding 50 at.% Pt and RTA transforms the film to a single L1₀ ordered tetragonal phase.
The L1₀ (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt phase exhibits high magnetocrystalline anisotropy and ~1000× coercivity increase.
The high anisotropy arises from reduced symmetry and strong spin–orbit coupling from Pt.
